name: a-flash-digicam-birthday
prompt: Vertical family snapshot from about 2002, shot on a cheap silver compact digital camera with a low-resolution CCD sensor, its tiny pop-up flash firing straight at the table: a crowded terraced-house lounge at night during a kid's sixth birthday. Framed tight and lopsided, horizon leaning to the right, the birthday girl sits low in the frame with a gappy grin and a crooked paper crown, lips pursed at five wobbling candles on a supermarket sponge cake smeared with blue icing. Behind her a scrum of cousins, a dad in a football shirt and a nan in a cardigan whoop with arms in the air; one lad sticks his tongue out, one aunt stares back with glowing red pupils. The flash flattens every face into bright shiny skin and blown-out white napkins, casts a hard black halo-shadow on the woodchip wallpaper, then dies within a couple of metres so the back of the room drops into a murky tangerine haze from a single standard lamp. Clutter crammed into the corners: helium balloons drifting against the artex ceiling, a party-ring biscuit plate, paper cups of fizzy pop, ripped gift wrap over a loud paisley carpet. Colour cranked and garish, warm-yellow cast, greenish noise blotches in the shadows, crunchy compression smearing the dark edges, a little soft from a plastic lens. Chaotic, loud, joyful. Leave the frame free of writing, date stamps, numbers or logos. Thanks.
